entities.summary: Johann Fust (1450-1466) was a German printer, publisher, and merchant in Cologne, Germany, who played a pivotal role in the development of the printing press and the spread of literacy in Europe. Fust's partnership with Johannes Gutenberg, the inventor of the movable-type printing press, revolutionized book production and dissemination, contributing significantly to the Renaissance and the Protestant Reformation. Fust's legacy extends beyond the printing press, as he helped establish the first printing press factory in Europe, paving the way for the mass production of books and the spread of knowledge during the 15th and 16th centuries. Fust's success also enabled him to invest in the arts, supporting local artists and musicians, and contributing to the cultural flourishing of Cologne during the late Middle Ages. In 1470, Fust sold his printing press to Peter Schoeffer, marking the beginning of the Schoeffer-Fust printing press, which would become a dominant force in European printing for centuries to come. This transaction is often cited as the first recorded instance of a printing press being sold, highlighting the growing importance of the printing press in the economy and society. Through his innovative business strategies and technological advancements, Fust transformed the way people accessed and disseminated knowledge, leaving a lasting impact on European society and culture.
